Hi team —

Thanks, and great to see the cluster coming up. I put together a short checklist and an initial SIEM mapping spreadsheet attached. High-level notes below so your security folks have context: 

- Export formats we support on private deployments: structured JSON over TLS (recommended), Syslog/CEF over TLS, and a bulk evidence bundle (signed tar) for airgapped handoffs.
- For Splunk ingestion we recommend JSON lines with the following top-level fields: timestamp, tenant_id (customer-provided), instance_id, stream (access|control|audit|trace), level, event_type, message, trace_id, span_id, sample_rate. See attached spreadsheet (neptune-siem-mapping.xlsx).
- Egress models:
  * Push (outbound push to a customer-owned collector endpoint): fewer firewall holes (single destination), lower ops on host side, requires customer collector certs.
  * Pull (Redwood SFTP/drive pull from an internal forwarder over a secure bastion): useful for stricter egress control but introduces scheduling and windowing constraints.

Firewall footprint (minimal):
- HTTPS/TLS to customer collector: ports 443 or 6514 (syslog-tls)
- NTP outbound (UDP 123) for timestamp sync (optional if you rely on local clocks)
- If using Red-initiated pull, allow inbound connections only to the bastion IPs we agree on (we can provide ephemeral keys).

Action items I propose:
1) Neptune security to confirm preferred export format (JSON over TLS vs syslog).
2) Neptune to provide collector FQDNs and certs (if push).
3) Redwood to provide signed mapping spreadsheet and a draft egress policy for review.

I've attached the mapping and a one-page egress draft. Laura — can you review the ports and add any compliance notes for retention? Marcus — can you add the tracehook example and a minimal conf snippet?

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks Kim — a few quick clarifications from compliance/security perspective: 

- Retention: Neptune requested 90 days hot + 1 year cold. That aligns with most regulated customers but requires proof of segmented storage for audit logs. We'll provide a retention appendix that outlines how retention tiers are enforced in the private runtime.
- Data minimization: recommend masking PII at the forwarder level. We'll provide a small config snippet for field-level redact before egress.
- Ports: 443 (JSON/TLS) and 6514 (syslog-tls) are the only outbound ports we should ask to open. Avoid arbitrary outbound SSH.

I'll attach the retention appendix as a short note and flag the masking snippet for Marcus to integrate into tracehook_example.conf.

Thanks — Laura

Adding the tracehook and a minimal forwarder config. Inline example below and attached a sample conf.

--- tracehook_example.conf ---
# forwarder config (json-lines over TLS)
forwarder.type = "json_tls"
forwarder.dest = "https://collector.neptune-east.neptune.io:443"
forwarder.tls = {
  ca = "/etc/ssl/certs/ca.pem"
  client_cert = "/etc/ssl/certs/redwood-client.pem"
  client_key = "/etc/ssl/private/redwood-client.key"
}
filters = [
  {type = "redact", fields = ["user.email","credit_card"]},
  {type = "drop", condition = "level == \"debug\" and stream == \"internal\""}
]
# tracehook: include trace_id/span_id in every log line if present
tracehook.format = "trace_id=%s span_id=%s"
--- end ---

Notes:
- The forwarder supports batching; configure batch size to 512 events or 200ms flush, whichever comes first.
- For airgapped handoff we produce a signed evidence bundle (tar.gz + detached signature).

I'll upload tracehook_example.conf as an attachment. Tessa — can you own the acceptance test steps for Splunk ingestion?

Cheers,
Marcus Lin
Principal SW Engineer, Serving Runtime
Attachment: tracehook_example.conf (conf)
